::: {.why}
This is the round your training makes you best at and the one you are most likely to over-answer, because the assessment is compression rather than depth.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Answer ten statistics questions in ninety seconds each, out loud, without exceeding the time.
- Identify the two answers where you went too deep and rewrite them shorter.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Ninety seconds each, ten questions, recorded. The constraint is the exercise: an answer that takes four minutes reads as a lack of judgement rather than as expertise, however correct it is.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Review the recording for the failure mode that is specific to you: starting from the general case and working toward the answer, rather than answering and then qualifying. Rewrite the two worst offenders in the answer-first form and record them again.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Add the one question you will be asked because of your background: how does genome-wide association work and why is the multiple testing problem there the same as in backtesting. Answer it in ninety seconds.
:::
:::

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
Ten recorded ninety-second statistics answers, with two rewritten in answer-first form.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Explain the multiple testing problem in a genome-wide scan and in a backtest, in ninety seconds, and say what is different between them.
:::
